title: Luminescent Erbium-Doped Silicon Thin Films for Advanced Anti-Counterfeit Labels

nodes.label: Anti-counterfeit labels need data that stays unreadable in an optical or scanning electron microscope

requires_unseen: the introduction and the statement of the counterfeiting problem are not in the packet; the need is read from the title and the F1 linked text

nodes.label: Selective fs-laser irradiation of an Er/Si bilayer should dope Er into silicon locally, giving 1530 nm luminescent pixels

requires_unseen: the 1530 nm emission wavelength, the fs pulse duration and the Er(20 nm)/Si(105 nm) bilayer are given in the F1 caption and linked text; the F1 crop carries no text at all

nodes.label: Bilayer film on silica: a 105 nm silicon host carrying a 20 nm erbium overlayer as dopant reservoir

attrs.image_note: F4a also draws an unlabelled ~10 nm layer above the 20 nm Er film that no caption in the packet explains

nodes.label: Absorbed fluence from 0.5 to 16 mJ/cm2, and fake-to-luminescent spot separation from 2 um in 0.5 um steps

requires_unseen: the 0.5 um separation step and the 2 um starting separation are stated only in the F3 linked text

nodes.label: Write fake spots at the same fluence beside and over the luminescent spots after etching

requires_unseen: the ~518 cm-1 peak position, the 520 cm-1 bulk-silicon reference and the small-grain reading of the deviation are stated only in the F2 linked text (refs 56-59)

nodes.label: Erbium is incorporated into the silicon matrix of the irradiated spots as optically active Er:O complexes

requires_unseen: the Er:O complex and its silicon surrounding are asserted in the F4 linked text (ref 65); the packet carries no compositional measurement

nodes.label: Above about 2.7 mJ/cm2 the Er3+ surrounding changes from crystalline silicon to oxygen-rich amorphous SiO2

nodes.label: The written spots have a rimmed, donut-like form with a partly emptied centre
Local laser heating crystallises the amorphous silicon and drives erbium in-diffusion from the overlayer into it

requires_unseen: the heating-and-crystallisation reading is given in the F2 linked text

nodes.label: Oxidation during irradiation in air surrounds Er3+ with oxygen, and Er:O in silica emits more strongly than Er in silicon

requires_unseen: the oxidation-in-air argument and the brighter Er:O emission are stated in the F2 linked text

nodes.label: Above the damage threshold the heated material evaporates, removing emitting film and emptying the spot centre

requires_unseen: the damage threshold and the evaporation argument are stated in the F2 linked text

nodes.label: Heat from writing a neighbouring spot makes erbium diffuse laterally, blurring and weakening the luminescent spot

requires_unseen: the erbium-diffusion reading of the blurring is stated in the F3 linked text

nodes.label: PL at 1530 nm grows with absorbed fluence, peaks near 8 mJ/cm2 and falls above it

requires_unseen: that the flat F4c trace named FaS is a spot written after the erbium layer was etched away is stated only in the F4 caption and linked text

nodes.label: Fake spots closer than about 2 um shift and blur the luminescence of the neighbouring luminescent spots

notes: No introduction, methods or results text (captions_plus_linked_text), so HYP, the deposition route and every numeric process parameter are 'text' with requires_unseen. The spine is the five-step label route (deposit -> write luminescent spots -> etch -> write fake spots) with the structure/mechanism chain n9 -> m1 -> n10 -> m2 -> n13 hanging off the first writing step; the crater-geometry claim (n12) and the etch-selectivity claim (n14) are the two side branches, and all three lines converge on the performance claim n17. Defects found by opening the images: (1) the F2 caption gives the Raman line as 578 cm-1 where the panel axis, the F2c ordinate and the F3b map all read 518 cm-1; (2) F2c and F3 use incompatible fluence scales - F2c has the crystalline Raman signal peaking near 3 mJ/cm2 and near zero above 8, while the F3 linked text puts the crystallisation threshold at 4.8 and the PL threshold at 5.5 mJ/cm2 and F3a/F3b show both still growing at 6.4 (audit node o16); (3) the F2d crop overlaps panel c - its OCR 'axis labels' 530nm(a.u.) and 'intensity' belong to F2c's right-hand ordinate; (4) the F3a OCR reads the third fluence label as '5' where the image shows 5.7; (5) the AFM inset of F4d is labelled 'Height (um)' with ticks 0, -75, -150 that must be nm, and its two single traces differ by about 25 nm in the opposite order to the quoted means, so 'indistinguishable in AFM' is only partly shown (o14, image_support partial); (6) F4 carries five panels a-e but the packet caption is truncated after (d) and no crops are offered, so panel (e) - the PL read-out of the QR code, the paper's headline result - is described nowhere in the packet text; (7) F4a draws an unlabelled ~10 nm layer above the 20 nm Er film that no caption mentions; (8) the crops F3b, F3c and F3d are Raman and PL maps but carry the OCR cue class 'micrograph' (from the 'um' scale-bar token), which the cue map forbids for RAMAN and PL, so those three panel citations were dropped in favour of the whole figure F3 with attrs.fig_ref.

split_nodes.why: the label joined two claims with a semicolon: the phase identity (crystalline silicon grains in the irradiated zones, evidenced by o1, o2, o8 with the k1 lookup) and the grain-size reading of the 518 vs 520 cm-1 deviation, which the F2 linked text attributes to the finite small size of the grains. n21 is STR/microstructure/feature_size, spine false, source text (no panel shows a grain size), fed by n9 supports and k1 premise_for.

a size claim and a form claim in one label, separately evidenced (o14/o6 for the dimensions, o7 for the donut) and separately explained (only the emptied centre is what m3, the evaporation pathway, accounts for). n12 keeps the lower id and becomes STR/microstructure/feature_size; n23 is STR/microstructure/shape, spine false, with n6 produces n23, o7 evidences n23 and n23 supports m3.

'luminescent spots keep their emission after etching' and 'spots written afterwards give none' are two claims about two objects with two causes: the HCl step (n7) leaves incorporated Er untouched, while the fake spots (n8) have no erbium left to incorporate. n22 is PRP/value (optical), spine false, caused by n8, evidenced by o12 and supporting n17.

pairs.cause: femtosecond laser irradiation of the double-layered Er/Si thin film
pairs.effect: formation of optically active erbium centres in a silicon matrix with crystalline phase
pairs.why: n6 (point-by-point fs-laser writing) produces n9 (crystalline silicon grains), evidenced by o1 (518-520 cm-1 peak appears after exposure, absent initially), o2 and the F3b map o8, with the k1 lookup; m1 (local laser heating crystallises the silicon and drives Er in-diffusion) explains n10 (Er incorporated as optically active Er:O complexes). Qualification carried in the graph: n10 is source=text (the packet has no compositional measurement) and the o16 audit records that F2c puts the crystalline maximum near 3 mJ/cm2, below the fluences at which the label is written.

pairs.cause: formation of optically active erbium centres in the crystalline silicon phase
pairs.why: n10 causes n13 (PL at 1530 nm grows with fluence, peaks near 8 mJ/cm2), evidenced by o3 and o4, with m2 explaining it. The graph qualifies the 'crystalline' half of the cause: n11 (above about 2.7 mJ/cm2 the Er3+ surrounding turns into oxygen-rich amorphous SiO2) is the joint second cause of n13, and o5 records that the fine structure MatMech attributes to a uniform crystalline environment is smoothed into one broad peak at the brightest condition, 8.9 mJ/cm2.

pairs.effect: stable and enhanced photoluminescence for anti-counterfeit label applications
pairs.why: n13 motivates the down-select n16 (record the 42x42 code at 6.6 mJ/cm2 with 2.5 um pitch, the 'enhanced' half), which realizes n17 (the label reads as a QR code in the 1530 nm PL map but as a featureless hole array in reflected light), evidenced by o13 and o15 and carried into the conclusion n18. The 'stable' half is only partly covered: the graph has n14 (emission survives HCl etching) but no node for stability under repeated reading, because the packet carries no read-cycle data (it is in the Supporting Information); n20 records the opposing limitation, the 2.7 um detection resolution.

pairs.cause: femtosecond laser irradiation creating luminescent and non-luminescent holes
pairs.effect: two types of anti-counterfeiting labels with different security levels
pairs.why: the spine is exactly this route: n6 writes the luminescent spots (first-type label), n7 etches the erbium layer, n8 writes the fake spots at the same fluence, n22 says those give no emission and n12/n23 say both kinds are the same crater, so o13 sees a uniform hole array in reflected light while o15 sees the QR code in the PL map (n17), and n18 states the two-level label. The fluence 6.6 mJ/cm2 and the 2.5 um pitch of the MatMech params are n16.
